newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway oil union to decide June 20 on wage talks.
newsitem.headline: Norway oil union to decide June 20 on wage talks.

text.p: The union for production and automation technicians working on Norway's offshore oil and gas platforms said on Thursday its regional representatives will meet on June 20 to decide whether to accept this year's wage offer or to enter a period of state-mediated negotiations.
The Norwegian Association of Supervisors (NALF) failed to agree a settlement with the Oil Industry Confereration (OLF) at talks in Stavanger on Monday and Tuesday.
Union leader Jan Olav Brekke said the deadlock was over compensation for workers due to an increase in workers' responsibilities and duties following a reorganisation of jobs on the platforms.
"The issue of compensation for our members has not been solved and our regional representatives will meet in a week to decide what to do next," Brekke told Reuters.

The Norwegian Oil and Petrochemical Union (NOPEF) and the Federation of Norwegian Oil Workers (OFS) already have accepted OLF's offer of a rise of 8,900 crowns per year and a two crown increase in shift allowance to 34 crowns per hour.
NALF has around 800 members working on most of the installations on the Norwegian continental shelf.
If NALF opts for state-mediated negotiations, the two sides will have one month to arrive at an agreement. If a deal is not cemented in that time, NALF could give a 14-day strike notice.
If a strike does ahead only Elf Petroleum's Heimdal and Frigg fields and British Petroleum's Ula and Gyda would be spared from any disruption.
